title: Decide the strict transfer hypothesis at the manuscript exponent (no new kappa)
body:
## What this establishes

The merged package `research/uniform-parking-psi` (PR #3528) evaluated the bit-motif parking node at `tau = 1/2`, found `Psi = 22587334999661/22587335000 > 1`, and left this as its open question:

> The manuscript states its transfer exponent as `1-2^{-50}`, not `1/2`. The next reading is whether this same child list has Psi below 1 at that exponent.

It does, on both manuscript recurrences.

The manuscript's parking schedule makes every child a rank-one call, so `t_i = 1` for every term, `J = s = sum_i t_i`, and

```text
Psi(tau) = (1 - eta) m^(1 - tau).
```

The strict hypothesis is therefore not merely sufficient but equivalent to `tau > tau*(eta) = 1 - ln(1/(1-eta))/ln m`. With `m = 10^6` and the two displayed relative rank deficits:

| node | `eta` | `Psi(1-2^-50)` upper bound | `tau*` deficit bracket |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| bit | `339/22587335000000` | `1 - 1.4996140048450776e-11` | `[1.0863449905681094e-12, 1.0863449905762616e-12]` |
| complex | `73/19906842167500` | `1 - 3.6548102269157696e-12` | `[2.6543216407854528e-13, 2.6543216407903196e-13]` |

A single exponent serves both recurrences, so the binding node is the complex one (`tau* = 1 - 2.65432e-13`); the manuscript's `1-2^-50` clears it by 298.85x.

Two consequences recorded in the package:

- The displayed constant `20` may be replaced by `ln m = 13.8155`, and the manuscript's comparison has slack 844.9 (bit) and 206.4 (complex).
- The displayed comparison is strictly weaker than the exact test: `1-2^-42` satisfies `Psi < 1` on both nodes but fails `eta > 20*2^-50` on the complex node. The recorded control exercises both verdicts.

## But do not overstate it

This is one exact scalar inequality per recurrence. It does not reprove the transfer theorem, does not change the manuscript's exponent, and does not touch any supplier, kappa or selected-frontier record. Two limits matter:

- The `O(e^tau)` conclusion carries `C/(1-Psi(tau))`, about `6.7e10 C` (bit) and `2.7e11 C` (complex). The statement is asymptotic; the finite base range is untouched.
- `Psi(tau) = (1-eta)m^(1-tau)` uses the rank-one schedule. A batched child list with some `t_i > 1` would make `sum_i (t_i/m)^tau` exceed `s/(W m^tau)`, and the displayed `s/W < m^tau` comparison would then no longer imply `Psi < 1`. That case is left open.

## Evidence

Package `research/parking-psi-exponent-threshold/`, base `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`, branch `research/w2-1018-parking-psi-threshold`.

- `verify.py` authenticates the three pinned inputs by SHA-256, re-derives `m`, `s_b`, `s_c`, `eta_b`, `eta_c` from their displayed source forms, checks both role counts are integers multiple of `m`, and computes rigorous rational brackets for `ln m` (atanh series plus geometric tail bound), `-ln(1-eta)` (positive series) and `exp(2^-50 ln m)` (`1+u <= e^u <= 1+u+u^2/(2(1-u))`). Every inequality is asserted exactly before any decimal is rendered; `--emit` regenerates `RESULT.json`.
- `independent.py` shares no series and no logarithm. It concludes the same result from `20*2^-50 < eta` by integer cross-multiplication, `log m < 20` from `m < 2^20` and `2 < e`, and `e^x <= 1/(1-x)`, plus a coarse threshold bracket with `log m` in `(13,20)`.
- `test_controls.py` runs twelve mutation groups: eight rejections (scaled deficits, `tau` at `1/2`, `9/10` and `1`, `1-2^-38`, an altered child count), the sharp boundary pair `1-2^-38` rejected against `1-2^-42` accepted, two positive runs, and the `1-2^-42` displayed-comparison rejection.

Commands, all passing under CPython 3.12 at `~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12`:

```text
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/parking-psi-exponent-threshold
  -> PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE ... outcome=completed
  -> PASS_PARKING_PSI_EXPONENT_THRESHOLD
  -> PASS_PARKING_PSI_EXPONENT_THRESHOLD_INDEPENDENT
  -> PASS_PARKING_PSI_EXPONENT_THRESHOLD_CONTROLS
python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/parking-psi-exponent-threshold --check-source-history
  -> PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES {"commit": "73113d754b6abaafafe07b3140a3fb0dddbb756c", "files": 12, ...}
```

A CI replay also ran the registered package job on the pushed head: [run 39156368643](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39156368643) finished `success`, with both the `plan` and `replay (research/parking-psi-exponent-threshold)` jobs completing successfully. That is the authoritative replay for this branch; the local run above is consistent with it.

## Overlap

`scripts/find_overlap.py "parking Psi threshold manuscript exponent recurrence motif"` returned `POSSIBLE_OVERLAP_NOT_A_NOVELTY_CERTIFICATE` with **0 possible matches**, coverage 432 open PR records and 2482 discussion records fetched 2026-10-18T18:52Z (complete pagination). That is bounded coverage, not a novelty proof.

## Credit

Nick Petalas. Produced by Nick Petalas with AI assistance. The `Psi` definition, strict-hypothesis lemma, rank-one schedule, both relative deficits, the exponent `tau = 1-2^-50` and the displayed comparison `eta > 20*2^-50` are the manuscript's, pinned by Git blob in `SOURCES.json`. The previous package `research/uniform-parking-psi` (PR #3528) is credited for the `1/2` evaluation and the open question. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.
